transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining on short notice. As you're all aware, we received an anonymous report alleging that a procurement vice president steered technology purchases toward a preferred supplier. Our preliminary review looked at the procurement policy, selected emails, and payment records, but reached no final conclusion. The audit committee has asked me to present a recommended resolution plan at its meeting this Friday. Under company practice, I need to obtain a final check from investigations, finance, employment, and insurance counsel before I can present that recommendation. I've asked you all here today so we can coordinate and make sure I have what I need from each of your areas before Friday. Let's start by going around the table — what can each of you tell me about what you've found so far and what you'll need to complete your respective reviews?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share an important update from the investigations side. After conducting two additional witness interviews this week, I've concluded that the procurement vice president did steer the purchases in violation of company policy. I have not yet finalized that conclusion in the preliminary review memorandum, but based on what I've gathered, the violation is substantiated. I wanted to make sure everyone here has that information as we each work through our respective areas of review before Friday.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: From the finance side, I completed a reconciliation yesterday that's not yet in the preliminary packet. I matched the supplier invoices against the approved purchase orders for the transactions under review, and I can confirm the company overpaid exactly $240,000 on those transactions. This quantifies the financial impact and will be relevant for the audit committee's consideration of the resolution plan.

transcript.text: From the employment side, I need to share something important. In a confidential meeting this week, the reporting employee told me that the vice president has begun excluding them from meetings after the report was made. My required protective plan is anti-retaliation monitoring with check-ins every 14 days for exactly 60 days. I have not yet added this to the investigation plan, but it needs to be included before Friday's audit committee presentation.

transcript.text: From the insurance side, I need to flag a critical timing issue. I've reviewed our D&O policy, and the circumstances surrounding this matter must be reported to the insurer within exactly 10 business days after becoming reasonably likely to produce a claim. Today is business day 6 since that threshold was met, and importantly, my policy review has not yet been circulated to the investigation team. Given Thomas has now substantiated the violation, we are squarely within that window. I recommend we prioritize getting the insurer notice on file immediately, and I'll need to circulate my policy review to the team today so everyone is aligned before Friday's audit committee meeting.
